name: Flirt
lede: Flirt is a deep purplish red, a name our library traces to the early twentieth-century color dictionaries rather than to any dye or flower.

sections.title: A name from a color dictionary
sections.body:
Our library files Flirt under the Maerz and Paul dictionary of 1930, as cited in the ISCC-NBS circular of 1955 [1]. Who chose the word, and why, is undocumented. The ISCC-NBS system calls the nearest block deep purplish red, about 7.2 units away on the CIEDE2000 scale [1].

No book in our collection treats the color [2][3]. The only hits are about the verb: one book notes that the English verb *to flirt* dates to the Middle English period and later passed into French as *flirter* [2], and another mentions a Goya sketch of a woman stopping to flirt [3]. Neither tells us anything about the shade, so the name's connection to the verb is a guess we do not make.

sections.title: How it sits among reds
sections.body: On screen the swatch reads as a dark, slightly blue red, close to [[magenta]] in direction but much deeper, and clearly further toward purple than [[crimson]] [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,781 paintings, a color this close appears in only 2 works, which makes it rarer than 82 per cent of the named colors [4]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, so a match is not a pigment test [4].
